China chip policy · the policy documents

The policy documents: 103 policy lines and 266 lines on local rules and provincial plans

Most are texts the Chinese state published. No published order against buying Nvidia chips was found among them. The review office's 2023 conclusion on Micron, which says operators of critical information infrastructure in China shall stop buying its products, is in the list. So such a text could have been found.

Draft by Claude, Anthropic's model.

Made from the project's checked note of policy documents (NOTE_policies_checked.md) with its table of quotations, and from the project's tables of provincial plans and local voucher rules (tables/provinces_31.tsv, local_vouchers.tsv, local_vouchers_more.tsv, with local_vouchers_classes.tsv and local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv). 103 lines of a list of policy leads; 83 saved pages; 208 passages in the pages' own words, 172 of them Chinese.

How to read a line

  • A line of the first 103 is one entry of a list of policy leads that an earlier search made. The project's checked note then read each lead in the saved copy of its page, and its check note says what it found; where a check note speaks of the list, it means that list of leads.
  • Found in the page means the saved page carries what the lead said (on line 100 of the list, in a chart of the page that was read by eye, as its check note says); it does not mean that what the page says is true. Found in part (5 lines) means some part of what the lead said is not in the page, or (on line 91) is in the page but not where the lead put it; the check note says which.
  • Words between quotation marks are the page's own, cut from the saved copy. The English under Chinese is ours, not an official translation. On 11 lines it is the project's corrected wording: the argument's (lines 8, 11, 25, 58, 63, 66, 74, 90 of the list) or the official record's (lines 9, 85, 91); on 12 lines (lines 2, 16, 17, 37, 47, 49, 50, 65, 67, 73, 84, 101) a few words of ours make a term or a target clear.
  • In a check note, words in italics are the note's own English, the list's own wording, or a reading the script could not check.
  • The date is that of the document or act as the list gives it; where the list gave none, the date the page gives (each such line says so). A script looked for it in the saved copy: it found date words for 100 of the 102 dated lines, and each line shows them.
  • On the lines from the project's tables, our reading gives what a rule pays for home-made computing (what the rules call 国产, home-made, or 自主 and 自主可控, independent and independently controllable) and what it pays for other computing, as the project's table reads the rule. Same under other computing means the words pay what is given for home-made computing whatever the chip; not stated means they give no separate rate for other computing. Where the words give a rate and name no chip for it, with no separate rate for other computing, the line gives it as the rate given, with no chip named (10 lines): the words do not say which chips qualify. A rule that “states no share of the bill” gives no number for the share it pays (some say only “a certain share”, 一定比例). The date shown on these lines is the first date the table's date cell gives (a signing, issue, posting or application date: the line's document field says which). Under the issuing body stands the saved page's title, or, where no page title is held with the saved copy, the document's name as the table gives it.
  • Saved copy gives the name under which the project holds each copy. The names were given when the copies were filed and carry that filing's labels (the name of the search that saved a copy, which may name another place, or a word such as unsaved or missing): they do not describe the copy, and the line says what each copy is.
  • Abbreviations: PUE, power usage effectiveness (a data centre's total power use over its computing equipment's); MIIT, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; AIGC, AI-generated content; SaaS, software as a service; OPC, one-person company.

Read with care

  • Two sources. 103 lines come from the checked note of policy leads. 266 more come from the project's tables of local rules and provincial plans, marked From the project's tables: all 31 provincial-level governments (9 were found to set a share for home-made computing, each by its plan's own measure: chips, equipment, hardware and software, or computing capacity; one of them, Zhejiang's, for the computing of one sector, its information and communications industry; 20 have a plan that was read and sets none; 1, Tibet, is known only from accounts of it, its issuer's own among them; for 1, Xinjiang, no computing plan's text was found, though the region's development and reform commission, in a reply posted Jul 24, 2026, says two were issued), and 235 rows of the project's tables of local voucher and subsidy rules whose words a script finds in a saved copy: 91 of them are in the project's count and 144 are not (by reason, the commonest: 32, an earlier or narrower rule of a government whose rule in force is counted; 26, an application guide, not the rule; 22, it states no share of the bill; and other reasons), and each line says which, as the project's table of classes gives it. 2 voucher rows are left out because none of their words could be checked by script (local_vouchers_more.tsv, row 102; local_vouchers_more.tsv, row 211): both saved copies are files without a text layer, as the table says. On the lines from the tables the English is the table's reading of the rule, not a translation. Counting one rule in force for each local government whose text is saved in a form that could be checked by script and which states a share of the bill, the argument finds 91 among the rules found by searches that went province by province and city by city, saved and read (not a census of every local government): 7 pay more for home-made computing and still pay for other computing (Binjiang, Chengdu, Hubei, Longwan and Wenzhou Bay New Area, Wenzhou, Wuhan, Zhejiang), 4, those of Sichuan province, Ningbo city, Huangyan district and the Changsha Economic and Technological Development Zone, pay for home-made computing only, and 80 state no higher rate for home-made computing: 79 pay one rate whatever the chip, and one, Hangzhou's, pays 30% or 20% by a type of computing facility that it does not name. One zone dropped its tier: Beijing's E-Town paid up to 40% and up to 30% under its rule of March 2024, and a later rule, of Nov 26, 2024, repeals that one and pays 30% whatever the chip.
  • Not every line is a government text. Of the 103 lines of the checked note, 69 are official texts, 13 are company filings or statements, 16 are press reports, and 5 are of other kinds (2 official texts or figures carried by news outlets; 2 lines from an advisory committee's roadmap; 1 think tank's translation of a government text). Each line carries its kind.
  • A press report is not published policy. What the press reports as Beijing's instructions to companies, it reports from people it does not name; no line here is a published order of that kind.
  • Found means said, not true. A passage that is found shows what the page says.
  • “Not found” is about these 369 lines only. Nothing here shows what was never published, or what was published and not gathered.

财政部关于印发《政府采购进口产品管理办法》的通知

Official textFound in the page

“第四条 政府采购应当采购本国产品,确需采购进口产品的,实行审核管理。”

Our EnglishArticle 4. Government procurement shall procure domestic products; where imported products are really needed, review applies.

3 more passages from this page

“第五条 采购人采购进口产品时,应当坚持有利于本国企业自主创新或消化吸收核心技术的原则,优先购买向我方转让技术、提供培训服务及其他补偿贸易措施的产品。”

Our EnglishArticle 5. In buying imported products the purchaser shall hold to the principle of helping domestic enterprises' independent innovation or their absorption of core technology, and give priority to products that transfer technology to our side, provide training or offer other offset measures.

“第七条 采购人需要采购的产品在中国境内无法获取或者无法以合理的商业条件获取,以及法律法规另有规定确需采购进口产品的,应当在获得财政部门核准后,依法开展政府采购活动。”

Our EnglishArticle 7. Where the product a purchaser needs cannot be obtained in China or cannot be obtained on reasonable commercial terms, or laws and regulations otherwise make imported products necessary, procurement proceeds only after approval by the finance department.

“2007年12月27日 财库[2007]119号”

Another provision for home-made computingfor AI computing facilities of 100P or more built in the city, at least 80% of whose rated computing runs on 自主 (independent) chips: help to enter the provincial and city project lists for provincial subsidies, and an operating subsidy of 50,000 yuan a year for each petaflop sold or used, the city's operating subsidies together up to 10 million yuan a year (part 3, item 1, the supply side (三、（一）加强普惠算力服务)). Its words: “支持物理空间和实体均在我市辖区内建设、算力标称值达100P以上”; “基于自主芯片的算力标称值占比不低于80%的人工智能算力基础设施项目申报列入省重点技改项目库或市级数字经济重点库，争取省级相关补助”; “按照实际销售和运营使用的算力规模”; “每P算力每年给予5万元运营补贴，市级每年累计算力运营补贴总额最高不超过1000万元”. From tables/local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv; the count above looks at the counted payment only.

Our reading, in Englishhome-made computing: for firms on the city computing platform buying from 100,000 yuan up to but not including 300,000 yuan a year (10万元（含）至30万元（不含）): 50% of the actual service fee in the first year, 40% in the second, 30% in the third (by year, not by chip); for 300,000 yuan or more, help in applying for the provincial subsidy, and the city pays the part above the provincial ceiling; up to 500,000 yuan a firm a year; other computing: same (no word for home-made computing in the clause); kind: subsidy on bought compute (补助). This is the project's table, not a translation.

“最高按照其实际购买金额的50%给予算力“服务券”

In the project's count?Yes; it states no higher rate for home-made computing; the argument counts it at one rate: it pays one rate, by its words, for one named centre, which Tianjin Daily calls wholly home-made. From the project's table of classes, tables/local_vouchers_classes.tsv, by its counting rule: one rule in force for each local government whose text is saved in a form that could be checked by script and which states a share of the bill.

Another provision for home-made computingan award of up to 20% of research costs, up to 5 million yuan, for AI research and applications built on Ascend (昇腾) and other 自主可控 (independently controllable) technology routes, once they are put to use in the district with returns (article 5 (第五条 支持关键技术创新)). Its words: “第五条支持关键技术创新。支持企业及各类组织围绕人工智能重点领域基于昇腾等自主可控技术路线开展科研攻关”; “对在河北区落地转化产生效益的，最高按照其实际研发费用的20%给予不超过500万元的奖励”. From tables/local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv; the count above looks at the counted payment only.

Another provision for home-made computingup to 50% of the new research equipment bought, up to 10 million yuan, for building 自主可控 (independently controllable) common-technology research platforms jointly with the Tianjin AI Computing Center (article 9 (第九条 支持建设共性技术研发平台)). Its words: “第九条支持建设共性技术研发平台。鼓励企业及各类组织依托天津人工智能计算中心联合建设自主可控的共性技术研发平台，最高按照平台建设新购置研发设备总价的50%给予不超过1000万元的资金支持”. From tables/local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv; the count above looks at the counted payment only.

Our reading, in Englishhome-made computing: up to 50% of what is actually bought from the Tianjin AI Computing Center, as computing service vouchers, up to 300,000 yuan a year; other computing: same (the clause names no chip; it pays only for computing bought from the named centre, which Tianjin Daily, on the city government's site, says runs 300P of purely home-made computing on Huawei's Ascend architecture); kind: voucher, bought compute (服务券). This is the project's table, not a translation.

Another provision for home-made computinga subsidy of up to 10% of the purchase, up to 10 million yuan, for buying and deploying intelligent-computing equipment whose chips' key core technology is 自主可控 (independently controllable) and broadly equal to comparable international products in function, performance and power use, or reaching the international lead on some of those measures (item 6: （六）自主智算能力跃升). Its words: “鼓励企业或机构采购并部署智算设备，其智算芯片的关键”; “核心技术自主可控，并在功能、性能、功耗指标上与国际同类产品基本相当，或部分指标达到国际领先水平”; “按照采购额最高10%给予补贴，总金额不超过1000万元”. From tables/local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv; the count above looks at the counted payment only.

Our reading, in Englishhome-made computing: 30% at most of what is spent renting computing, for open-scene projects (50% at most for international data business; up to 80% of the contract for small and medium technology firms and start-up teams, with small caps); up to 10 million yuan a project; apart from rental, up to 10% of the purchase of intelligent computing equipment that is also deployed, whose chips have independently controllable key technology and roughly match international products of the kind in function, performance and power use, or lead on some measures; other computing: same for rental; none for the purchase subsidy; kind: rental subsidy; purchase subsidy. This is the project's table, not a translation.

“对采购智能算力服务和模型服务的用户企业，一般按不超过合同实际发生金额的30%给予补贴”

“使用算力设施开展模型训练、推理和应用的，按照算力设施的不同类型给予30%或20%的分档补贴”

“对于年申报智算合同累计金额50万元（含）以下的中小企业，按照不超过50%的比例给予补贴”

“试行智能券政策，对采购智能算力服务的企业、高校、科研机构，给予合同发生金额的30%或10%分档补贴”

“如另行申请杭州算力券，可叠加补贴比例至60%或30%”

“本方案自2025年7月15日起施行”

In the project's count?Yes; it states no higher rate for home-made computing (two rates by a type of computing facility that the rule does not name). From the project's table of classes, tables/local_vouchers_classes.tsv, by its counting rule: one rule in force for each local government whose text is saved in a form that could be checked by script and which states a share of the bill.

Our reading, in Englishrate given, with no chip named: up to 30% in general for the Hangzhou computing voucher; for training, inference and applications on computing facilities, 30% or 20% "by the type of computing facility", types the plan does not define; up to 50% for small and medium firms whose declared intelligent-computing contracts add up to 500,000 yuan a year or less; up to 8 million yuan a firm a year, a cap the plan lets firms making generative multimodal foundation models exceed; a trial intelligence voucher (智能券) pays 30% or 10% in tiers it does not define either, stacking to 60% or 30% where the city voucher is applied for separately (15% or 10% from the city voucher where its matching is taken without review, 免审配套); other computing: not stated apart (the voucher clause names no home-made, independent or other computing; the measures of 2024 that this plan repealed set the same two rates, 30% and 20%, for home-made and for other facilities, and the draft of this plan named home-made and other computing); kind: voucher on bought intelligent computing and model services; trial intelligence voucher. This is the project's table, not a translation.

Another provision for home-made computinga condition on the supplier: the voucher pays for renting the computing of admitted suppliers (算力开放单位), each of which must be able to serve on home-made chips with a home-made software stack; it pays up to 25% of the contract whatever chip the service runs on (article 17, item 2 (with article 16)). Its words: “租用开放单位的算力设备”; “第十七条 符合条件的算力设备拥有单位，经申请、审核、公示后成为算力开放单位，鼓励其为使用算力创新券的企业提供优惠，须同时满足以下条件”; “可基于国产芯片并使用国产软件栈提供算力服务”. From tables/local_vouchers_other_provisions.tsv; the count above looks at the counted payment only.

Our reading, in Englishhome-made computing: up to 25% of the contract's actual amount; up to 500,000 yuan a year for firms in benchmark incubators or in technology-business incubators whose provincial or ministerial (or higher) recognition is still valid (有效期内的省部级及以上科技企业孵化器), and 200,000 yuan for other medium, small and micro technology firms; a computing supplier must be able to offer its service on home-made chips with a home-made software stack (a condition on the supplier: not a higher rate, and not a rule that only such service is paid); other computing: same; kind: voucher on rented computing for small technology firms (one part of the city's science and technology innovation voucher). This is the project's table, not a translation.

No line holds those words. The search reads the date, the issuing body, the title, the passages, our English, the check note, the address and the saved id.

Every quotation on this page was looked for in its saved copy by a script, which found all of them: 737 quoted strings checked (passages, date words and the words check notes quote), 737 found, none missing; and the script's two tests of itself came out as they must (a sentence planted as false was not found in its saved copy, and a true one was). Of them, 302 are on the 103 lines of the checked note (their passages, the same strings, row by row, as in the note's own table of quotations, 207 strings plus the two of the line read in a second copy; their date words; and the words their check notes quote) and 435 on the 266 lines from the tables. A passage that is found shows what the page says, not that it is true.

Left out: 1 passage of the note under six characters long (line 28 of the list), which the script that checks quotations does not test.

Our English is the checked note's, shown without the quotation marks that note puts round a few terms: only a page's own words stand between quotation marks here. On 11 lines it is the project's corrected wording: the argument's (lines 8, 11, 25, 58, 63, 66, 74, 90 of the list) or the official record's (lines 9, 85, 91); on 12 lines (lines 2, 16, 17, 37, 47, 49, 50, 65, 67, 73, 84, 101) a few words of ours make a term or a target clear.

The 266 lines marked From the project's tables come from tables/provinces_31.tsv, local_vouchers.tsv and local_vouchers_more.tsv: each passage shown was found by the same script in a saved copy the row names; the English beside them is the table's reading, not a translation (on the nine province lines that set a share, the share is given in the argument's words, as each of those lines says); the address is the one held with the saved copy.

The descriptions of the issuing body and the check notes are the checked note's own words, carried over by the script, except in a few places where this page puts them plainly: where the note names its list of leads, this page says the list; the note's row numbers are given as lines of this list; the note's first person is left out; where a check note said that words stood in the page but not in the project's text copy of it, this page says only where they stand in the page; three check notes gain a clause (what the passages from the think tank's translation are; that the evaluation announcement does not say what its levels mean; the ministry a press relay names); and the line on the evaluation centres' lists is shown as read in the centres' own page, which the project now cites. Li Chao is named as each page names him: the commission's own transcript gives his name and his office, the policy research office (李超; 政研室), and Xinhua's report on the government's site, gov.cn, calls him the commission's spokesman (新闻发言人). Page titles are those held with the saved copies (a site's separator left at a title's end is not shown). Addresses are those the note gives.
